newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's AMP to mull demutualisation plan July.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AMP to mull demutualisation plan July.

text.p: Australia's largest institutional investor Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) said on Wednesday it expected the board to consider a plan for its late 1998 demutualisation in July this year.

"We expect that the board will consider this document at its meeting in July and if it is happy with it, we will approve for distribution to members," chairman Ian Burgess told the group's annual meeting.
Burgess said AMP's two million members should expect to receive an explanatory memorandum sometime in September, in advance of a November 20 meeting to vote on the plan.
Burgess said AMP had A$9.16 billion of retained profits at the end of 1996, of which A$7.8 billion is members' capital.
"This will become shareholders capital if we demutualise," Burgess said.
Burgess also commented on AMP's unsuccessful bid for the Scottish Amicable insurance group in Britain.
He said the commercial world contained many "bad shipwrecks" where companies had paid too much for a signifcant acquisition.
"So we are not too disappointed even though the margin above our bid was surprisly small," he said.
"I am glad to report that our lot showed restraint and discipline. There may well be another day. There are other companies like Scottish Amicable about but we are in no particulkar hurry," he said.
